page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The processor operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 120 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core processing is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 3051.87 and high single-threaded compression throughput, including 33.02 GB/sec in gzip and 14.81 GB/sec in bzip3. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, matching the single-core score at 3051.87 due to the shared CPU allocation and single physical core limitation. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks, reaching 46.78 GB/sec read and 44.33 GB/sec write, but weak for small cached blocks. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also positioned in the lower tier, with Redis achieving 3.44 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for static web serving, which registers an average throughput of 6.5 GB/sec, as well as lightweight single-threaded processing, caching layers, and development environments. It is less suitable for multi-threaded parallel processing, heavy database operations, or complex LLM inference, where its shared CPU architecture and low multi-core scores present clear performance bottlenecks.
